email.subject: Service credit request: GitHub Enterprise Cloud, Oct 2026
email.body:
Hi GitHub team,

We're requesting a service credit for GitHub Enterprise Cloud for October 01 to January 01, 2027.
Your SLA (GitHub Enterprise Service Level Agreement) promises 99.9% uptime a quarter, or 10% back at or below 99.9%, 25% back below 99%.
Your public status page shows 1201.8 minutes of outage in that period, for 99.093% uptime:
- Nov 13 15:47 UTC, 162.3 min, Incident with Pull Requests (https://stspg.io/qzj7qjdcr8jc)
- Nov 11 20:48 UTC, 33.5 min, Impact across multiple GitHub products including Actions, Pages, and Copilot products. (https://stspg.io/jdjlq5zjyl48)
- Nov 10 16:10 UTC, 104.2 min, Incident with Git Operations and Pull Requests (https://stspg.io/16nsnk2th3rv)
- Nov 09 18:12 UTC, 46.9 min, Incident with Actions and Checks API (https://stspg.io/7yw63xl9ztrv)
- Nov 09 10:00 UTC, 110 min, Incident with Webhooks and Actions (https://stspg.io/4vdghm7tycm4)
- Nov 04 17:40 UTC, 35.6 min, Incident with Actions (https://stspg.io/7pwv28hvkmz8)
- Nov 04 16:05 UTC, 55.7 min, Incident with Actions and Pages (https://stspg.io/pjgptg3cfc6n)
- Nov 04 09:49 UTC, 120.2 min, Incident with Pull Requests, Git Operations and Issues (https://stspg.io/18blsgwnbyy6)

That puts the credit at 10% of 6,300.00 USD, so 630.00 USD.
The period isn't over yet, so this is the minimum: downtime so far already breaks the promise.
Please apply it to our next invoice and confirm by reply.

Thanks,
our team

proposal.proposed_procedure:
# claim-writer

## Instructions

Write a short, firm, polite service-credit claim email to the vendor based on the audit.

1. Check the vendor playbook and apply relevant lessons.
2. Identify the applicable SLA and quote the exact clause and service-level promise. Do not paraphrase the quoted clause.
3. List every incident included in the claim. For each, provide its date, start time, resolve time, counted minutes, status, and status-page link. Ensure the link is clearly associated with that incident.
4. State the credit percentage and dollar amount, based on the audit and applicable SLA. Do not invent missing details or calculations; identify information that is missing or ambiguous instead.
5. Ask the vendor to apply the credit to the next invoice.
6. Keep the email specific to the audit, and verify that the clause, incident details, links, percentage, and amount are present and consistent before returning it.
